suggestions.assertion: Generated wiki page has frontmatter with non-empty title, type set to 'concept' (or one of concept|index|synthesis|claim|template), sources listing the ingested file, created + updated ISO dates, a non-empty summary, and 4-8 content-only tags
suggestions.reason: All pages have quality: 0.0 in frontmatter. This may be the default stub that lint/quality_score is supposed to replace, but no assertion forces quality to be recomputed > 0. An executor that skips quality scoring entirely would still pass. Consider asserting quality > 0 (or that a quality_score step was invoked).

suggestions.assertion: events.jsonl records separate entries with op='init', op='ingest', and op='query' (one per operation), all with ISO timestamps
suggestions.reason: The ingest event records total_tokens_in=0, total_tokens_out=0, total_cost_usd=0 and agent_calls=[]. Either the harness didn't make LLM calls (unlikely given 5 rich pages were synthesized) or token accounting isn't wired through. No assertion catches this silent instrumentation gap.

No assertion checks that the 'How to Go Deeper' footer (live/raw/db shortcuts) is present and its raw-source link resolves. The recent G-ORM-DEEPER commit added this convention; without an assertion, regressions would go unnoticed.

No assertion verifies that the source file copied into raw/ byte-for-byte matches the ingested input. A silent truncation or re-encoding could pass today (the current check only asks that it be 'copied'). sha256 parity against the input would be stronger.

eval_feedback.overall: All 12 tightened assertions pass cleanly with substantive evidence — the output is genuinely high-quality (grounded facts, resolving citations, proper provenance), not coincidentally compliant. The hardeners (op=init present, citations resolve, concrete facts cited, valid provenance) all hold. Remaining gaps are around token-accounting instrumentation and raw-copy byte parity, not around the core behaviors under test.
